I went with rotating refresh tokens stored hashed in Postgres. Each use invalidates the old token and issues a new one, and reuse of a revoked token revokes the whole family.
The trade-off is one extra write per refresh, which is fine at current traffic. The alternative was stateless long-lived tokens, which can't be revoked.
Let me know if you want the stateless approach instead.
